title: security-role-word lint skips fields declared through objectExtensions, so a field named role passes validate, build and verify
body:
qa#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUARzLeR7GhKms8a5s

QA-source: #31433 comment 6754602020 · scenario:service_desk · build

Found by the QA seat's scenario half (round record: comment 6754602020 on #31433; subject `0647dabb`, `--packages workspace`). The service_desk authoring agent hit the reserved-word refusal on an object field and declared the same field through an object extension instead, on purpose, and said so; the app then built and booted with the reserved name.

## Reproduction

1. In an app, declare `defineObjectExtension({ extend: 'NS_agent', fields: { role: { type: 'select', label: 'Group Function', options: [...] } } })` and register it under `objectExtensions` in `defineStack`.
2. Run `objectstack validate`, `build` and `verify`: no finding; the app boots with `NS_agent.role`.
3. Contrast: the same field in the object's own `fields` fails with "security-role-word … uses the reserved word 'role' (ADR-0090 D3)".

## Mechanism

`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` line 1643, `validateSecurityRoleWord`: it walks `recordsOf(stack.objects)` and each object's `fields`, `actions` and `fieldGroups`, plus permissions, positions, apps and books. It never walks `stack.objectExtensions`, though the same file already has `objectExtensionsByTarget` (used around line 771). One door refuses a name another lets through: the shape the rule's own docstring forbids. Not measured: whether the runtime publish gate has the same gap.

Severity as read: low (a governance rule bypassed; no data exposure).

Owning package: `@objectstack/lint`.
